p.d: In order to learn and master Terastallization, Liko, Roy, and Dot have joined the Naranja Academy's "Tera Training"! Armed with the ambition, necessity and idealism of youth, Charlize, Kheng, and Sani enter the Prison Service with very different goals. Behind prison walls, the rookies quickly learn that the job is not just about discipline and control, but trust, rehabilitation and second chances. They will learn some of their most valuable lessons about life, love and sacrifice from the people they least expect — inmates, colleagues, ex-convicts and their families.

Best Telenovela - National Winner Asian Academy Creative Awards (2020) | Kin is a drama about the complexities of life, love and family relationships. Years have passed since Yoke and Ella had their lives turned upside-down when they returned to be with their rightful families after having been swapped at birth. Years later, Yoke has seemingly embraced her role as a status-conscious, high society Shelley, assuming a leadership role in the family business. Ella has accepted her fate as a member of the salt of the earth, working-class Loh family but struggles to make something of her life. Has the nature vs nurture battle run its course or are relationships between the families still as fraught and complicated as ever? The Lohs, Shelleys, Hassans, and Balas have overcome personal loss, incarceration, as well as estrangement of their loved ones; yet lingering tensions remain. Mysteries continue to unfold as characters pursue their individual agendas, while emotional drama abounds as surprising twists are revealed that threaten the stability to which they have become accustomed..

Brand new series where the UK's most passionate cooks get a once-in-a-lifetime chance to launch their own food brand to the British public. Cooking Up a Fortune sees amateur foodies, who dream of escaping the rat race and cooking for a living, create and sell their dishes to hundreds of real diners in a purpose-built food arena. Each week the winning kitchen gets to launch their idea for a food business to paying customers in one of Europe's busiest food markets.

Three generations of the Jin family live under one roof. Mrs. Jin-Ke mei-man has two sons, You-Tsai and You-De. You-Tsai abandoned the family many years ago, leaving his wife Siou-Ying to shoulder the huge responsibility of the Jin family business selling fish products at market. Although Siou-Ying was betrayed by You-Tsai, she has still been a dutiful daughter to her mother-in-law, and has single-mindedly raised four children. 三代同堂的金家，奶奶金柯美满，膝下有两子-有财跟有德。有财早年抛弃家庭离开，妻子秀英一肩扛下金家重责大任，在市场从事贩卖鱼货的工作。虽然有财对不起秀英在先，但秀英仍然孝顺婆婆，也拉拔彦钧等四个孩子长大。透过金家的故事，除了体会婚姻的酸与甜，还得面对婆媳、姑嫂、妯娌间的「那些小事」…，也透视到家庭与爱情真正爱的真谛！

p.t: Helen Dorn: The Right To Remain Silent
p.d: During a hunting trip, Rolf Kanther, director of a military tech manufacturer, is shot right next to his daughter. Inspector Helen Dorn is sent to investigate the suspicious death, and needs to find out if it's an accident or a calculated murder.

Ranging from a 60-year-old retiree who no longer finds herself desirable to a daughter trying to make her breakthrough as a model, five women of different ages confront their self-image and the expectation they have for themselves and the people around them.

p.t: In Other Circumstances: The Missing Child
p.d: Some children go missing long before they disappear. When eight-year-old Sascha vanishes, suspicion tears through his broken family. But as every secret surfaces, Commissioner Winter discovers the greatest danger isn't who took the boy—it's the home he came from.

Felix enjoys his single life to the fullest, but a ferret bites him, sterilizing him in the process. He tries everything in his power to find the soon-to-be mother of his only child, the result of his first and last sperm donation.

An author's success following the release of her celebrated erotic memoir is threatened when her best friend and muse reveals the truth behind the memoir's provenance, igniting an incendiary tale of sex, lies and betrayal.

Anna is a 35-year-old single mother, working hard as a paramedic to provide a better future for her daughter Katia. A sudden turn of events makes Anna question her moral compass in a society where everyone has lost their own.

p.t: The Boy Who Wants To Live
p.d: 70-year-old Willi catches Malian refugee Nama stealing, but decides not to report him. Having been a refugee once, Willi sees a part of himself in Nama, and brings him home. However, Nama’s decision further frays his relationship with his son.

Extraordinary People pays tribute to unsung heroes who make a profound impact through selfless acts of compassion, often overcoming personal challenges along the way. This docu-series shines a light on individuals championing under-the-radar causes. Through their own initiatives, they support underserved communities such as lonely seniors, marginalised groups and persons with special needs and disabilities, tackling issues like mental health, inclusivity and equity.

Welcome to Singapore Hour: your all-access pass to the city that never stops surprising. From iconic eats to cutting-edge tech, vibrant culture to hidden local gems – we bring you the best of Singapore through the eyes of those who know it best. Whether you’re here to travel, work, or just soak up the vibe, Singapore Hour is your definitive guide to what’s hot, what’s next and what you absolutely can’t miss.

By Your Side follows families caring for loved ones with rare diseases, special needs, disabilities and the challenges of ageing. Parents of children with West syndrome and Harlequin ichthyosis navigate seizures, intensive treatments and daily care while celebrating every small achievement. Mothers of adult sons with ADHD, autism and intellectual disabilities devote years to helping them gain confidence, skills and independence. The series also follows families facing ALS and dementia, where spouses and children provide constant care as their loved ones gradually lose their independence. Across generations, these caregivers sacrifice careers, time and personal freedom, yet find strength in love and companionship. Their stories celebrate resilience, acceptance and the preciousness of simply being by someone's side.

In this returning season of FINDING, six heartfelt reunions honour people who left a lasting mark. Nearly 40 years after Basic Military Training, Minister Ong Ye Kung searches for his BMT buddy Eric, while actor-host Noah Yap reunites with Ma’am Haiyan, the mentor who believed in him and supported his family through difficult times. Actor Elvin Ng and his mother travel to Indonesia to surprise Jumi, the domestic helper who became their pillar of strength, while 23-year-old Leticia journeys to Central Java to thank Auntie Mas, who helped raise her for 12 years. Dino Isaac reconnects with the Primary 3 teacher whose kindness gave him hope after a traumatic childhood, while radio DJ Gerald Koh and conservation educator John Chua surprise the teachers who inspired and guided them. Together, these emotional journeys celebrate friendship, gratitude and the lasting impact of those who quietly shape lives.

Jalan Lain gives light to 8 remarkable profiles with their own stories to tell. Some would have decided that a life in arts would be better suited to their skills, some would have realised that couldn't bear working in an office environment. They would have all different upbringings and unique lives, but all these profiles would eventually make their mark in a truly unconventional manner. The series will cover their stories from their early struggles but it would also trace their steps from thereon - and how they conquered life on their terms. With a host at the helm, the series will also take a deep dive into these profile's current lives and their work. The host will play their part in trying to get a much deeper understanding of what these profiles do for a living and how - with the host partaking to see if they have the ability to keep up even though they excelled in their own education.

But even masters need to stop and refuel. When meals or snack time interrupt Ollie’s play, he finds himself confronted with the real challenge of childhood; trying new food. 13-year-old Peru is an only child who lives with his mother and grandmother. With his father is seldom in the picture due to his work overseas, a hardworking mother and a kooky grandmother, an awkward comic-loving Peru is left to his own devices as her navigates growing up in a quaint Singapore neighbourhood. One fateful day, through sheer coincidence, Peru finds himself in the living room of the three men-children who for some reason have no problem letting this young kid hang out with them. Arun - the food reviewer, Vijay – the job-hopper and Jagdish – the illustrator make up the menagerie of Peru’s new group of friends. Part immaturity, part aloofness of the three men makes Peru feel like an equal and he begins to open up to them. Peru comes to the house with his growing pain of the week. It’s unusual if the three bachelors actually offer any solutions, but Peru definitely inspires the three men to reflect on their lack of maturity and together the four of them grow up together. The four of them embark on a meaningful journey of friendship that will change their lives forever.

Arun - the food reviewer, Vijay – the job-hopper and Jagdish – the illustrator make up the menagerie of Peru’s new group of friends. Part immaturity, part aloofness of the three men makes Peru feel like an equal and he begins to open up to them. Peru comes to the house with his growing pain of the week. It’s unusual if the three bachelors actually offer any solutions, but Peru definitely inspires the three men to reflect on their lack of maturity and together the four of them grow up together. The four of them embark on a meaningful journey of friendship that will change their lives forever.
